preamble: The phonetic transformation from the diphthong /ue/ to the monophthong /o/ involves the simplification of a rising diphthong into a single, close-mid back rounded vowel. This process, known as monophthongization, often occurs in unstressed or weakly stressed syllables, or in specific lexical items, and is characteristic of colloquial or dialectal speech.

examples.note: Colloquial reduction of the discourse particle pues; the rising diphthong [we] coalesces into the back rounded vowel [o].
In very colloquial Murcian /ue/ in pues is monophthongized to /o/, realized open [ɔ] because the following /s/ is lost; the same reduction occurs in other southern Spanish accents.

sources: Monroy, R., & Hernández-Campoy, J. M. (2015). Murcian Spanish. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 45(2), 229–240. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100314000231
